FOREWORD This Indian Standard (Second Revision) was adopted bythe Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft Iinalized by the Secondary Cells and Batteries Sectional Committee, had been approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council. This standard was first published in 1976 and was first revised in 1982. This revision has been prepared covering the updated general requirements and methods of tests for lead-acid storage batteries based on available technology and experience gained so far. Specific requirements and tests for particular applications are specified in individual specifications. All the tests specified in this standard may not be applicable to all the batteries. In case any difference exists between this standard and the individual specification the provisions of the latter shall apply. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised).' The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

IS 8320 : 2000

Indian Standard GENERAL REQUIREMENTS AND METHODS OF TESTS FOR LEAD-ACID STORAGE BATTERIES ( Second Revision )
1 SCOPE 1.1 This standard specifies the general requirements and methods of tests for lead-acid storage batteries. The general requirements and tests applicable to batteries for special applications, such as aircraft, marine and miners, cap-lamp are not covered in the standard. 2 REFERENCES
Example :

When a cell/battery is so discharged to a specific end voltage that it delivers its rated capacity in IO-h, the rating is known as 10-h rating and is designated as Cl0 rating. Similarly 5-h rating (C5) would mean that the cell/battery delivers its rated capacity in 5 h. 4.1.1 The preferred Ah rating shall be as given in the individual specification. 4.1.2 For guidance, the capacities at various rates of discharge and the corresponding final voltages are given in the individual specification. The rate of discharge depends on the rated Ah capacity. The rate of discharge in amperes shall be obtained by dividing the specified Ah capacity by the rated duration in hours. 4.2 Nominal Voltage The voltage of each cell shah be 2 V. The preferred voltages for batteries shall be as given in the individual specification. 5 MATERIALS 5.1 Container The materials for container and lid shallbe as given in Table 1. 5.2 Electrolyte The sulphuric acid and water used for the-preparation and maintenance of electrolyte shall conform to IS 266 and IS 1069 respectively. 5.3 Sealing Compound The sealing compound when used in sealed or closed cells, and if bitumen based, shall conform to IS 3 116. 5.4 Separators The synthetic separators shall conform to IS 6071. 6 CONSTRUCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS 6.1 Cell Lids The requirements for cell lids shall be as given in the individual specification, 6.2 Venting Device The venting device shall be of anti-splash type and shall allow the gases to escape freely but shall 1

3.0 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in IS 1885 (Part S), in addition to the following, shall apply. 3.1 Type Tests - Tests carried out to prove conformity with the requirements given in the standard. These are intended to prove the general ' quality and design of a given type of battery. 3.2 Acceptance Tests - Tests carried out on samples selected from a lot for the purpose of verifying the acceptability of the lot. 3.2.1 Lot - All batteries of the same type, design and rating, manufactured by the same factory during the same perio-d, using the same process and materials, offered for inspection at a time shall constitute a lot. 3.3 Routine Tests battery. 3.4 Individual Specification - A specification that lays down the requirements and tests which are applicable to a particular type of battery and makes a reference to this standard for general requirements and methods of tests. 4 RATlNGS AND DESIGNATION

IS 8320 : 2000 6.7 Spray Arresters The open-cells shall be provided with spray arresters of adequate area over the plates. These may be of glass sheet at least 3 mm thick or some suitable plastics sheet and shall be adequately supported. 6.8 Any other constructional requirements applicable to the particular types of cells and batteries shall be specified in the individual specifications. 7 DIMENSIONS, LAYOUT AND MASS 10 CONDITIONS OF SUPPLY 10.1 To facilitate procurement of the correct type of cells and batteries, it is recommended that user should furnish the information about his requirements, given in Annex B at the time of enquiry or order. Similarly, the manufacturer should furnish the information given in Annex C. 11 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS FOR TESTS 11.1 Temperature for Tests Unless otherwise specified under various tests or in the individual specification, the temperature for tests shall bebetween 20�C and 35�C preferred temperature being 27 + 2�C. 11.2 Test Requirement 11.2.1 Voltmeter The voltmeter used for tests shall be of an accuracy class not inferior to 0.5 in accordance with IS 1248 (Part 2). The resistance of the voltmeter used shall be at least 1 000 ohms per volt. The range of the voltmeter used shall be such that the magnitude of the voltage to be measured falls in the last third part of the scale. 11.2.2 Ammeter The ammeter used for tests shall have an accuracy class not inferior to 1.0 [see IS 1248 (Part 2)]. The range of ammeter used shall be such that the magnitude of the current to be measured falls in the last third part of the scale. 11.2.3 Thermometer A thermometer with an appropriate scale shall be used for measuring temperature and one division of the graduated scales shall represent 1�C maximum. The accuracy of the calibration shall be not worse than 05�C. 11.2.4 Hydrometer The specific gravity of the electrolyte shall be measured by hydrometer provided with a graduated scale, one division of which shall represent 0.005 maximum unit of specific gravity. The accuracy of calibration shall be not less than 0.005 unit of specific gravity. 11.3 First Charge The cell/battery shall be first charged according to the manufacturers' instructions and when fully charged the level and specific gravity of the electrolyte of each cell shall be checked and adjusted if necessary. The electrolyte level shall be that recommended by the manufacturer and shall not be less than 6 mm over top of separators. 11.4 Specific Gravity of Electrolyte The specific gravity of the electrolyte shall be as specified in the individual specification. 3

NOTE - The specific values of `a' to `f' referred under this test method shall be given in the individual specification.

capacities obtained by multiplying with conversion factor expressed as percentage of the rated capacity. 12.8 Test for Loss of Capacity on Storage This test shall be carried out to determine the loss of capacity of a fully charged cell/battery left on opencircuit for a specified period. The test shall be carried out on a cell/battery which has passed the capacity test specified under 12.7.
NOTE - The values of `0' and `b' referred below shall be specified in the individual specification.

12.7.1 The battery shall be given the first charge as specified under 11.3. 12.7.2 After standing on open-circuit for not less than `a' hours and not more than `b' hours from the completion of first charge, and at an electrolyte temperature between 20 to 35"C, the cell/battery shall be discharged through a suitable variable resistance at a constant current of `c' amperes. The discharge shall be stopped when the closed-circuit voltage across the cell/battery falls to `d' x `n' volts ivhere `n' is the number of cells in the battery and `d' is the end voltage for each cell. If however, a test discharge can not be conducted within-the specified rest period due to any exigencies, a freshening charge may be given to the cell/battery at normal charging rate recommended by the manufacturer for a period of 1 h for every 24 h or part thereof of the extended rest period. The capacity test, however, can be started after a minimum period of 2 h elapsing after this freshening charge. 12.7.2.1 During discharge, hourly voltage readings shall be taken until the closed circuit voltage across cell/battery terminals approaches `e' x `n' volts, after which the readings shall be taken every 15 min until the voltage falls to a voltage `f' volts. 12.7.3 The temperature of electrolyte shall be taken hourly and the average temperature PC shall be taken as the temperature of electrolyte during discharge. 12.7.4 The cell/battery shall be charged at the normal charging rate immediately after the discharge. 12.7.5 The time in hours elapsing between the beginning and the end of discharge including the last period of 15 min during which the voltage first fell to `1' volts shall be taken as the period of discharge. This period of discharge multiplied by the constant discharge current `c' amperes shall be the Ah capacity of cell/battery at PC which shall be corrected to 27�C in accordance with 11.5. 12.7.6 Requirement The capacity shall be within 100 and 120 percent of the rated capacity declared by the manufacturer. The 120 percent limit is however, not applicable to other 5

12.8.1 The batteryshall be fully charged at the current specified, by the manufacturer and it shall then be submitted to two consecutive capacity tests in accordance with 12.7, the value of initial capacity being calculated as the mean of the two results thus obtained shall be denoted by C. 12.8.2 After a complete recharge and after cleaning of the electrolyte from its surface, the cell/battery shall be left on open-circuit for a period of `u' days without disturbance at a temperature of 27 + 2"C, unless otherwise specified in the relevant specification. 12.8.3 After storage for a period specified in 12.8.2 the cell/battery shall be discharged in accordance with 12.7. The value of capacity measured after storage shall be denoted by c' . 12.8.4 After the discharge, the cell/battery shall be fully charged at the rate recommended by the manufacturer. 12.8.5 The loss of capacity S expressed as a percentage, shall be calculated from the formula:
s = C-C' x loo

NOTE - There are two methods for determining life of c& battery. The choice of Method A or B be specified in the individual specification.

12.14.4.1 The cell/battery shall be discharged at `a' amperes for `6' h and charged at `c' amperes for `d' h. Such discharge/charge cycle shall be carried out `e' number of times.
NOTE - The duration of discharge and charge may be such that two cycles of discharge and charge be possible per day.

12.14.3 Method A 12.14.3.1 The cell/battery shall be subjected to a series of successive charges and discharges. The current `a' amperes for discharge and `b' amperes for charge and duration `c' h for discharge and `d ' h for charge. 12.14.3.2 After the last charge of `e' cycles of discharge, the cell/battery shall be disconnected from the circuit and shall be left in tank on open-circuit for a period of `f' h. After open-circuit stand as specified in 12.14.3.2 the celhhattery shall be subjected to a discharge test at `g' amperes to a cut-off voltage of `h' volts x `n' where `h' is the voltage per cell and `n' is the number of cells in a battery. After the completion of this discharge the battery shall be fully recharged. If for any reason the open-circuit stand period `j' h as specified in 12.14.3.2 is exceeded by 2 h, the cell/ battery in the water bath may at the option of manufacturer be kept on trickle charge at a current I = 0.01 x (Rated Capacity) Amperes until the time of test discharge.

12.14.4.2 After each services of `e' cycles, the cell/ battery shall be fully recharged and capacity shall be checked in accordance with 12.7.

12.14.4.3 After the capacity test as specified in 12.14.4.2 the cell/battery shall be fully charged and the cycles of discharge and charge shall be resumed. 12.14.4.4 The life test shall be complete when on a test discharge, in accordance with 12.14.4.2, the obtained capacity falls below `n' percent. 12.14.4.5 Requirement The total number of discharge (including discharge) shall be not less than `p'. 12.15 Vibration Test Respective individual specification shall specify test schedule where applicable. 12.16 Bump Test Respective individual specification shall specify test method and requirement, where applicable. 12.17 Storage The unfilled cell/battery shall be stored for a period of `u' months (to be specified in the individual specification) at the room temperature after which it shall be tested for capacity in accordance with 12.7. ANNEX D
(CZause 12.1.4)
SAMPLINGSCHEME AND CRITERIA FOR ACCEPTANCE

D-l D-l.1

SCALE OF SAMPLING Scale of Sampling

The number of batteries to be selected at random from the lot shall be in accordance with co1 1 and 2 of Table 2. In order to ensure the randomness of selection, random number tables shall be used (see IS 4905). D-l.2 The batteries selected as above shall be subjected to the acceptance test in the order specified in the individual specification. Each of the batteries selected in the first stage in accordance with co1 2 of Table 2 shall be tested for

acceptance tests. A battery shall be declared defective if it fails in one or more of the acceptance tests. If the number of defectives is less than or equal to C, the lot shall be considered as conforming to equal to or greater~than C, the lot shall be considered as not conforming to the requirements of the standard. If the number of defectives in the first stage is less than C, and greater than C,, a further sample of same size as taken in the first stage shall be taken and tested. If the number of defectives in the two samples combined is less than C,, the lot shall be considered as conforming to the requirements of the standard, otherwise the lot shall be considered as not conforming to the requirements of the standard.

Bureau of Indian Standards BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Strindards Act, 1986 to promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country. Copyright BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. Review of Indian Standards Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for~revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Handbook' and `Standards: Monthly Additions'.
